title: Meta-rdk: Preprocessed EEG data
description: Preprocessed EEG recordings from 20 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder and 22 healthy control participants performing a visual random-dot motion discrimination task. Participants reported motion direction by mouse reaching and then rated their confidence on a visual analog scale, with motion coherence individually adapted by a staircase procedure to match performance between groups. The dataset supports investigation of perceptual decision-making and metacognition in schizophrenia.
methods_description: Participants judged whether 100 moving dots in a central circle moved left or right, responding by clicking one of two targets with a mouse. Motion coherence was adapted individually with a 1up/2down staircase. After each decision, confidence was reported on a vertical visual analog scale from 0% (sure incorrect) to 100% (sure correct). EEG was recorded with 63 scalp channels using g.tec equipment. Schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorders were diagnosed with the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5.
